Dashboard MCP at https://api.dashboard.plaid.com/mcp/, hosted by Plaid, OAuth client_credentials with mcp:dashboard scope, limited support, Production-only. Official but Dashboard-scoped. A local AI coding toolkit (sandbox) also exists in plaid's GitHub.
ready_with_caveats is consistent: self-serve sandbox, real data gated by Trial/Production, Link UI needed per user, MCP not covering data APIs.

corrected.one_liner: Plaid is a financial data network and API platform that lets apps connect to users' bank accounts for account data, transactions, identity, balances, and payments.
corrected.auth_notes: Per Plaid's API docs, almost all endpoints take a client_id and secret, in the request body or in the PLAID-CLIENT-ID and PLAID-SECRET headers. Per-user bank access goes through Plaid Link, which produces a public_token that is exchanged for an access_token. That Link and token exchange flow is not described on the fetched pages. The API reference page does not mention OAuth. The Dashboard MCP server uses OAuth client_credentials tokens, a separate mechanism from the main API.
corrected.access_notes: Sandbox is free and fully featured, and keys come from the Dashboard. Some products, such as UK/EU Payment Initiation, need a request for access. For real data, teams created on or after 2026-04-15 (US and Canada only) get a Trial plan. Older teams may be on Limited Production, which is deprecated and has caps. Full Production is applied for through the Dashboard. The fetched pages do not state the approval criteria. Pricing was not checked.
corrected.blocker: The Sandbox is self-serve, but real bank data needs a Trial plan or Production approval. Each end user must also complete Plaid Link in a client UI before the agent has an access_token. Some bank connections (Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo) require full Production access plus OAuth registration. The official MCP server only covers Dashboard diagnostics and analytics, not the data APIs. It is production-only and has limited support.
